Standard: At all allowable attitudes, and under steady state and transient engine operation throughout the engine operating envelope, the engine pressure balance system prevents: a. Bearing damage or reduction in stated bearing life from null loading, bearing crossover, skid, or other operating characteristics. b. Damaging vibration and DR for both installed and uninstalled engine operation. c. Vibration or DR that inhibits the flight crew from effectively accomplishing required functions during installed operation. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Analysis results indicate that loads imposed on the engine bearings assure bearing operation without damage. Bearing loads are checked across the full range of engine operating modes, operating conditions, power settings, and flight conditions. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Bearing rig tests confirm individual bearing load capability and durability.
  (2) Lab test: Full-up instrumented (bearing loads and engine vibration) engine testing ensures engine bearing radial and thrust loading is within design limitations and ensures operation of the bearing and rotor support system. Engine test is conducted in an altitude test cell to simulate altitude and ram conditions representative of operational use. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (3) Flight test: Vibration testing confirms that vibration characteristics are non-damaging and do not inhibit the flight crew from effectively accomplishing required functions, and that vibration magnitude does not exceed defined engine or air vehicle limits.
